payload.title: TCA 51% but MFU Under 8%: Hidden GPU Performance Losses
payload.summary: An investigation into the surprising gap between Tensor Core Activity (TCA) and Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU), uncovering clock frequency scaling, tile padding waste, and instruction-level inefficiency as root causes.

sections.heading: 1. Background
sections.gist: TCA (Tensor Core Activity) is the fraction of clock cycles during which the Tensor Core is active.

sections.heading: 2. GPU Architecture Overview
sections.gist: A GPU comprises multiple Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs).

sections.heading: 3. MFU vs TCA: The Expected Relationship
4. Power Wall and Clock Throttling
sections.gist: Running large matmul benchmarks on B200 revealed MFU consistently below TCA, with MFU capped at ~83.22% regardless of matrix size.

sections.heading: 5. Tile Padding Waste
sections.gist: When matrix dimensions are not integer multiples of the tile size, cuBLAS pads to tile boundaries.

sections.heading: 6. Flash Attention 2 Makes TCA Artificially High
